learning_objective: 🎯 Master the art of 'Touch Typing', understand keyboard layouts, calculate typing speed, and learn proper computing ergonomics to prevent health issues.

key_vocabulary.definition: Typing without looking at the keyboard, relying purely on muscle memory.
The middle row of keys (A, S, D, F and J, K, L, ;) where your fingers rest.
The science of designing the workspace to fit the user, ensuring comfort and preventing injury.
Words Per Minute; the standard measurement of typing speed.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A standard QWERTY keyboard has Alphanumeric keys (A-Z, 0-9), Punctuation keys (, . ;), Modifier keys (Shift, Ctrl, Alt), Navigation keys (Arrows, Home, End), and Function keys (F1-F12).

Your left fingers rest on ASDF and right fingers on JKL;. The 'F' and 'J' keys have small physical bumps on them so you can find your starting position without looking. Your thumbs rest on the spacebar.

Correct posture is vital. Monitor should be at eye level, 20-24 inches away. Keep your back straight, feet flat on the floor, and elbows bent at a 90-degree angle. This prevents RSI (Repetitive Strain Injury) and back pain.
Speed is measured in CPM (Characters Per Minute) or WPM (Words Per Minute). A 'word' is standardized as 5 characters or keystrokes. Gross Speed is total words typed; Net Speed subtracts the errors.

fun_activity.title: 🙈 The Blindfold Typing Challenge
fun_activity.instructions: Place your index fingers on the 'F' and 'J' keys (feel the bumps!). Close your eyes and try to type your name. Open your eyes to see what you wrote. Muscle memory takes practice, but once you learn touch typing, you'll type faster than you can write with a pen!

exam_tips: 📌 Guide Keys (F and J) are a very frequent short-answer question. Mention that they help position hands without looking.
📌 Always define Ergonomics in terms of user health, posture, and workspace arrangement.
📌 Numeric keypad data entry requires using the right hand, with the index finger on 4, middle on 5, and ring finger on 6.
quick_recap: ⭐ The keyboard layout used universally is called QWERTY, named after the first six letters on the top left row.
⭐ The 'Shift' key is a modifier; it modifies the output of another key when pressed together.
⭐ Accurate typing is more important than fast typing when initially learning touch typing.
